summary: Tested (A) Organization Public Join Link feature end-to-end, (B) Async course generation fix for Cloudflare-524, (C) mark-orphans idempotency, and (D) iteration-47 regression + /api/payments/status. Backend pytest: 15/16 passed on the new iteration 49 suite (with one intermittent latency observation on POST /api/courses/generate-custom — passed on isolated retry). Iteration 47 regression: 10/10 passed. Frontend: /join/<slug> renders and signup submits successfully; /org-admin/members shows all 3 tabs and all 7 settings testids (join-url, join-copy-btn, join-qr, join-enable-toggle, join-approval-toggle, join-domain-input, join-domain-add). Also found one real bug: POST /api/org-admin/create-course-from-pdf rejects super_admin role (only checks org_admin/admin), unlike the org-join routes which correctly allow super_admin.

critical.issue: Endpoint gate at server.py line 7741 is `role not in ['org_admin','admin']`, which returns 403 for super_admin. Inconsistent with all other /api/org-admin/* routes (org_join, join-settings) that now include super_admin. Blocks super admin from creating PDF-sourced courses and blocks E2E verification of the (B) Cloudflare-524 fix for the PDF path. Fix: add 'super_admin' to the allowed roles list, or replace the inline check with the `require_org_admin` dependency wrapper defined at server.py:14665.

minor.issue: POST response time was 16.9s on first run (over the 15s target) but 14.5s on isolated retry — occasionally borderline vs Cloudflare's 100s limit. Still well under 100s so the primary fix is holding. Consider warming the emergentintegrations LLM client on startup to eliminate cold-start latency variance.

action_items: Fix POST /api/org-admin/create-course-from-pdf to accept super_admin role (server.py line 7741). Swap the inline role check for the existing `_require_org_admin` dependency for consistency with the join-link routes.
(Optional) Warm-up LLM client on startup to keep generate-custom POST comfortably under 15s even on cold requests.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is now 14,874 lines — still needs modularisation; the fact that role-check drift (super_admin allowed in join routes but not in create-course-from-pdf) exists is a direct symptom of this size.

Two different auth patterns co-exist for org-admin endpoints: (a) inline `if role not in [...]` at each endpoint (fragile — bug found here), and (b) the `_require_org_admin` dependency wrapper. Pick one; the dependency wrapper is safer.

/api/courses/generate-custom and /api/org-admin/create-course-from-pdf use asyncio.create_task() with no persistence — if the process restarts during generation the course is stranded in 'generating' forever. Consider a background job table or a startup task that reaps stale generating rows > N minutes.
In org_join_routes.public_org_signup, password strength check is only length>=8 — no complexity requirement. Fine for MVP but should be documented.

org_join_routes _get_org_by_slug falls back to scanning ALL organisations linearly when neither join_slug nor slug matches — O(N) per public request; add a slugified-name index or backfill join_slug for all orgs.

success_rate.frontend: 100% for the tested flows (join page + org-admin members console)

seed_data_creation: Test users test.pending.*, test.reject.*, test.auto.*@example.com and test courses 'Test Course Async …' / 'Test Course PDF …' were created and CLEANED UP after tests (4 users, 2 courses deleted).
context_for_next_testing_agent: After main agent fixes create-course-from-pdf role gate, re-run pytest backend/tests/test_iteration49_org_join_and_async_courses.py::TestAsyncCourseGen::test_pdf_course_fast. All other iteration-49 tests are green. The org-join UI is fully wired with all documented data-testids.
rca of the issue: Bug: POST /api/org-admin/create-course-from-pdf returned 403 to super_admin. Reproduction: `curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer <super_admin_token>' -F 'file=@a.pdf' -F 'title=X' <BASE>/api/org-admin/create-course-from-pdf` → 403 {'detail':'Organization admin access required'}. Root cause: hard-coded role check at server.py:7741 `if current_user.get('role') not in ['org_admin', 'admin']` — super_admin not included. Contrast with server.py:14666 `_require_org_admin` which correctly whitelists ('org_admin','admin','super_admin'). Mitigation: replace the inline check with `Depends(_require_org_admin)` or add 'super_admin' to the list.
